title: Generative AI and Jobs: A Refined Global Index
limitations: Clerical work has high exposure; the paper expects transformation to be more common than complete replacement. Exposure is not a forecast of layoffs, and is not an estimate of your hiring chances.

title: Software developers, QA analysts, and testers
limitations: The current page projects 10% combined employment growth during 2025–2035 and describes typical degree requirements. US employment projections do not establish Bangladeshi salaries, entry-level demand, or remote access.

title: Generative AI at Work
limitations: The published study of 5,172 customer-support agents finds a 15% average productivity gain, with substantial differences between workers. This is task- and workplace-specific, not a universal AI effect.

title: Changing the developer productivity experiment
limitations: The early-2025 randomized study found a slowdown among experienced developers. The 2026 update describes biased later samples and weak evidence about the size of speedup; it cautions against treating the old estimate as current universal truth.

title: Reforms, jobs, and the geography of opportunity
limitations: Documents employment challenges and concentration of industrial jobs in Dhaka and Chattogram. Broad economic evidence does not validate a particular business niche or wage.

title: Software Engineering Internship (Backend)
limitations: Lists backend fundamentals, SQL, APIs, testing and critical review of AI output. Described as paid, with no salary amount. A single employer listing is neither market-representative nor independently verified; availability can change.

title: Software Developer: internship to full-time
limitations: Describes business systems and a modern web stack, with a conditional pathway to employment. This is an employer’s description, not a placement guarantee, salary benchmark, or endorsement.

title: Energy demand from AI
limitations: The base case projects substantial data-centre electricity growth to 2030. Outcomes depend on efficiency, adoption and infrastructure. This does not establish returns for a power stock or a small business in Dhaka.

title: Energy workforce and skills shortages
limitations: Describes expanding electricity employment and skilled-worker bottlenecks, with different conditions across technologies and countries. Global shortages do not remove local licensing, training or wage constraints.

title: Heat, health, and economic risk in Bangladesh
limitations: Uses temperature trends and a 2024 household survey to document heat-related impacts. Supports investigating cooling and adaptation needs, but does not establish willingness to pay for any proposed product.

title: Ageing and health
limitations: Projects that one in six people globally will be aged 60 or older by 2030. Care needs vary by place, purchasing power and policy. More need does not automatically mean better pay.

title: Consolidated export foreign-exchange rules, Part K
limitations: Part K, printed pages 36–37 (PDF pages 43–44), covers individual service exporters, electronic evidence, authorized dealers and compliance. Later circulars may modify it; ask your authorized-dealer bank to apply the rules to your actual payment route.

title: Visa options for IT professionals
limitations: Explains degree-based and experience-based routes and the importance of a job offer. Recognition, salary and other conditions apply. This is an example of credential option value, not a promise of eligibility.

title: Asset allocation, diversification, and rebalancing
limitations: Supports diversification, horizon-based allocation and awareness of concentration. US account types and legal protections do not transfer automatically to Bangladesh.

title: Understanding investment fees
limitations: Explains how fees affect long-term portfolio value. Product charges, tax and availability must be checked locally.

title: Do stocks outperform Treasury bills?
limitations: Historical research documents how a small share of stocks drove aggregate wealth creation. Supports caution about picking winners; does not establish future returns or apply directly to Bangladesh land.

title: Investor education and authorized intermediaries
limitations: Local starting point for capital-market education and investor protection. Registration is not a guarantee against investment loss.

title: Income tax FAQ
limitations: Official starting point for filing and taxpayer information. This guide does not assert that all freelance income is tax-exempt or calculate your tax liability.

title: Introduction to Programming with Python
limitations: A structured introduction with exercises and a final project. Course completion alone does not prove independent engineering ability; respect its academic-honesty rules.

title: Writing your first Django app
limitations: Official introduction to a web framework. Use documentation matching your installed supported version.

title: Learn web development
limitations: Reference and curriculum for web fundamentals; select HTML, CSS and basic JavaScript modules first.

title: PostgreSQL tutorial
limitations: Relational database and SQL fundamentals. Practice with your own schema and queries.

title: Web application security risks
limitations: A security awareness resource. Reading it is not equivalent to a security audit or professional certification.

title: GitHub Skills / Learn
limitations: Hands-on version-control and collaboration exercises. Focus on branches, commits and pull requests.

title: The Python tutorial
limitations: Reference for programmers new to Python. Use the beginner course first if programming fundamentals are weak.

title: Young workers and AI exposure: revised employment evidence
limitations: Reports a relative employment shortfall for young workers in highly exposed roles, chiefly associated with reduced hiring. The authors explicitly reject a causal interpretation and discuss education, pre-trends and sample limitations. It is not a Bangladesh forecast.

title: Job creation and structural transformation: Annex V
limitations: Annex V, printed pages 46–49, uses Bangladesh Labour Force Survey data to discuss educational attainment outpacing high-quality job creation. Broad structural evidence cannot price the return to an individual institution or predict a personal outcome.

scope: Dhaka · advertised role, not verified hiring
title: Junior Software Developer
limitations: Advertises BDT 25,000–30,000 per month, completed CSE degree, PHP/React/Next.js and databases. Payroll, salary composition and actual vacancy were not independently confirmed. One offer is not a wage distribution.

title: Support Engineer Fresher
limitations: Advertises BDT 20,000 monthly, degree preferred and strong English. Mentions rotating shifts and also standard office hours; clarify this inconsistency. Actual vacancy and payroll unverified.

date: Accessed 9 Nov 2026; no deadline on role page
title: Junior SQA Engineer
limitations: Describes 0–1 year experience, testing fundamentals and a preferred degree. Pay is described as competitive with no amount; it remains unknown. Do not borrow a deadline from another role on the careers page.

title: Inbound Sales & Product Demo Executive
limitations: Calls for English communication, product demonstrations and selling ability; welcomes freshers, but lists degrees and elsewhere prioritizes skills. Pay is undisclosed; eligibility and terms require clarification. Same employer as source 29, so not independent employer evidence.
